results.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press (45 Degree View)

anatomical: Clavicular Head of the Pectoralis Major

instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45 degree angle. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and hold the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
Maintain a firm grip on the barbell to ensure control and proper alignment.
Use a spotter if lifting heavy weights to ensure safety.
results.description: Barbell Incline Bench Press (45 Degree View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Landmine Chest Press
instructions: Stand facing the free end of the landmine barbell with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the end of the bar at chest height using both hands. Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body and brace your core.
Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended while maintaining a stable, upright posture.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping your shoulders down and your chest engaged.
Slowly lower the bar back to chest level under control and repeat.
tips: Press the bar in its natural arc rather than trying to move it straight overhead.
Keep your elbows slightly tucked instead of flaring them outward.
Keep your core engaged and chest up, avoid leaning backward.
Exhale as you press the bar upward and inhale as you return.
results.description: Barbell Landmine Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Serratus Anterior, Core.

results.name: Barbell Larsen Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your legs fully extended in front of your body and hold the barbell with a grip wider than shoulder width.
Keep your core tight and slowly lower the barbell to the middle of your chest while keeping your legs raised.
Pause briefly with the barbell lightly touching your chest.
Press the barbell back up until your arms are straight, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs fully extended and off the floor throughout the exercise, while engaging your core for stability.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
Press the barbell in a smooth, controlled path over your chest and lower the weight slowly with control.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you press it up.
results.description: Barbell Larsen Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Pause Incline Bench Press
instructions: Lie on an incline bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the bench. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and hold it directly above your chest with your arms fully extended. Engage your core and keep your shoulders retracted.
Slowly and with control, lower the barbell to your upper chest, pausing for 1-3 seconds when it lightly touches your chest.
Press the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the barbell up and inhale as you lower it down.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to reduce strain on your joints.
Focus on engaging your chest, shoulders, and triceps throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Pause Incline Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Smith Chest Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench positioned under the smith machine barbell, with your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the bench. Grip the barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell by extending your arms straight up. Having the barbell over your chest with your elbows slightly bent.
Lower the barbell towards your chest by bending your elbows, ensuring the barbell follows a straight path and your elbows are at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your elbows, fully engaging your chest muscles. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Maintain a 45-degree angle with your elbows to effectively target your chest muscles.
Avoid locking out your elbows at the top of the movement to keep tension on your chest.
results.description: Barbell Smith Chest Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a smith machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Spoto Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly on the floor and hold the barbell above your chest with a shoulder width grip.
Lower the barbell slowly until it is just above your chest without allowing it to touch.
Pause briefly for 1 - 2 seconds while keeping the barbell steady above your chest.
Press the barbell back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and pressed into the bench, and your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Maintain a straight bar path over your chest throughout the movement.
Keep the barbell just above your chest without letting it touch to maintain tension on the triceps. Pause briefly at the bottom of each repetition before pressing upward.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you press it upward.
results.description: Barbell Spoto Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

results.name: Cable Core Palloff Press
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the handle with both hands at chest level.
Press the handle straight forward until your arms are fully extended while resisting the cable's pull.
Pause briefly with your arms extended and keep your torso stable without rotating.
Bring the handle back to your chest with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating during the movement.
Brace your core before pressing the handle forward.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
Inhale as you bring the handle toward your chest and exhale as you press it forward.
results.description: Cable Core Palloff Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Fly Machine Mid
instructions: Set both pulleys at chest height and stand in the middle holding a handle in each hand.
Step forward with a slight bend in your elbows and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Return slowly to the stretched position and repeat.
tips: Keep the elbow angle fixed throughout.
Squeeze your chest when the handles meet.
results.description: Cable Fly Machine Mid is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Machine Low to High
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at a low position. Grasp the handles with your palms facing upward and arms extended at your sides. Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly staggered for stability.
Stand upright with your back straight. Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and palms should face upwards.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders as you lift the handles.
results.description: Cable Machine Low to High is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Chest Dip Bodyweight
instructions: Grip the parallel bars and lift yourself into a support position with your arms straight.
Lean your torso forward slightly.
Lower yourself until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Press back up to the start and repeat.
tips: Leaning forward shifts the work onto your chest.
Don't drop too deep if it hurts your shoulders.
results.description: Chest Dip Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders.
